threats.title: Credential stuffing and brute-force attacks
Offline cracking of stolen password hashes
Weak or previously breached passwords
Account enumeration
Session fixation after login
OAuth login CSRF and authorization-code interception
One-time code guessing and SIM-swap interception
Account takeover with a single compromised factor

controls.title: Hash passwords with Argon2id (or bcrypt/scrypt as fallback)
controls.ai_rule: Hash passwords only with Argon2id from a maintained library (bcrypt or scrypt if unavailable); never use MD5/SHA-* for passwords and never store or log a plaintext password.

verify.description: No md5/sha1/sha256 calls applied to password variables.
Stored password values begin with the $argon2id$ prefix.

controls.title: Rate-limit and throttle authentication attempts
controls.ai_rule: Every login, OTP-verification and password-reset endpoint must be rate-limited per account and per IP; never write an authentication endpoint without throttling.

verify.description: N+1 rapid failed logins for one account are rejected or delayed.
Auth route handlers are registered behind a rate-limit middleware.

controls.title: Enforce minimum length and block breached passwords
controls.ai_rule: Password policy: minimum 12 characters, maximum at least 64, no composition rules, and reject passwords found in breach lists; validate on the server, not only the client.

verify.description: An 11-character password and a known-breached password are both rejected.

controls.title: Issue a new session identifier on login
controls.ai_rule: On successful login or privilege change, regenerate the session ID / issue new tokens and invalidate the previous session.

verify.description: Session cookie value changes after a successful login.

controls.title: Use Authorization Code flow with PKCE and validate state/nonce
controls.ai_rule: OAuth/OIDC: use Authorization Code + PKCE (S256), verify state and nonce, validate ID-token signature/iss/aud/exp, never use the implicit flow or an embedded WebView.

verify.description: No response_type=token (implicit flow) in OAuth requests.
Callback rejects a request with a missing or mismatched state.

controls.title: Short-lived, single-use, rate-limited one-time codes
controls.ai_rule: One-time codes: generate with a CSPRNG, expire in 10 minutes or less, single use, invalidate after 5 failed attempts, compare in constant time.

verify.description: A used or expired code is rejected; the 6th wrong attempt invalidates the code.

controls.title: Offer multi-factor authentication (require it at higher assurance)
controls.ai_rule: Design authentication so a second factor (passkey/WebAuthn or TOTP) can be enforced; admin accounts must always require MFA.

verify.description: MFA enrollment exists and is enforced for admin roles.

controls.title: Return identical responses for unknown and existing accounts
controls.ai_rule: Login, signup and password-reset responses must not reveal whether an account exists: same message, same status code, comparable timing.

verify.description: Reset request for unknown vs. known email returns identical status and body.

controls.title: No security questions or password hints
controls.ai_rule: Never implement security questions or password hints for account recovery.

verify.description: Recovery flow uses a time-limited token sent to a verified channel only.

threats.title: Token theft through XSS when tokens are readable by JavaScript
Token leakage over the network, in URLs or through insecure cookies
Sessions that never expire or cannot be revoked
Forged or tampered JWTs (alg=none, algorithm confusion, weak signing keys)
A hijacked session is used to take over the account (change email or password)

controls.title: Strict JWT verification and short-lived tokens with rotating refresh tokens
controls.ai_rule: Verify JWTs with an explicit algorithm allow-list and check exp, iss and aud; never decode without verifying; keep access tokens short-lived and rotate refresh tokens with reuse detection.

verify.description: No jwt.decode used for authorization, no verify without algorithms option.
Tokens with alg=none, a wrong audience or expired exp are rejected.

controls.title: Keep browser tokens out of localStorage
controls.ai_rule: Never store access or refresh tokens in localStorage or sessionStorage; keep them in memory or use HttpOnly cookies via a backend-for-frontend.

verify.description: No localStorage/sessionStorage.setItem with token-like keys.

controls.title: Idle and absolute timeouts; server-side logout and revocation
controls.ai_rule: Sessions need an idle timeout and an absolute lifetime; logout and password changes must invalidate sessions or refresh tokens server-side, not just delete them on the client.

verify.description: A session token used after logout is rejected.

controls.title: Never put session tokens in URLs
controls.ai_rule: Never put session tokens, access tokens or API keys in URL paths or query strings.

verify.description: No token/session/api_key query parameters built into URLs.

controls.title: Re-authenticate before sensitive account changes
controls.ai_rule: Changing email, password, MFA settings or payout details must require re-authentication (current password or fresh MFA), even within a valid session.

verify.description: Password change without the current password is rejected.

controls.title: Let users see and end their active sessions
controls.ai_rule: Provide a way for users to list their active sessions and revoke any of them.

verify.description: The account settings page lists sessions and revoking one invalidates it.

threats.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
Clickjacking
Traffic downgraded to HTTP or intercepted (SSL stripping, mixed content)
A compromised third-party script runs with full page access
Open redirects used for phishing or token theft
Sensitive pages cached by browsers or shared proxies

controls.title: Encode output by context and avoid dangerous DOM sinks
controls.ai_rule: Never use innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, eval or new Function with dynamic data; rely on framework escaping, and sanitize with DOMPurify when HTML is unavoidable.

verify.description: No dynamic data flows into HTML sinks or eval.

controls.title: Strict Content Security Policy
controls.ai_rule: Do not add inline scripts or event-handler attributes; scripts load from our origin or carry the CSP nonce; never add unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval to script-src.

verify.description: HTML responses carry a CSP without unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval in script-src.

controls.title: Security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy)
controls.ai_rule: Keep the security-headers middleware on every response (HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy) and never remove or weaken it.

verify.description: Responses include HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy.

controls.title: HTTPS everywhere, no mixed content
controls.ai_rule: Load every resource and call every API over https://; never hardcode http:// URLs except localhost in development.

verify.description: No http:// resource or API URLs other than localhost.

controls.title: Minimize third-party scripts and pin them with Subresource Integrity
controls.ai_rule: Prefer npm packages over CDN script tags; any external <script> must have integrity and crossorigin attributes unless the provider forbids SRI.

verify.description: External script tags carry integrity attributes.

controls.title: Allow only safe, relative redirect targets
controls.ai_rule: Never redirect to a URL taken directly from user input; accept only relative paths starting with a single "/" or an allow-listed destination.

verify.description: No res.redirect() with request parameters.

controls.title: Prevent caching of sensitive responses
controls.ai_rule: Responses containing personal or sensitive data must send Cache-Control no-store.

verify.description: Account pages respond with Cache-Control no-store.

threats.title: Broken object-level authorization (accessing other users' records by ID)
Broken function-level authorization (calling admin or other privileged endpoints)
Mass assignment and excessive data exposure
Unrestricted resource consumption
Injection through unvalidated input
Cross-origin data theft through permissive CORS
Internal details leaked through errors, debug modes or version headers
Forgotten, undocumented or old API versions left exposed
Credentials or tokens exposed in URLs

controls.title: Check object-level authorization on every request that takes a resource ID
controls.ai_rule: Every handler that loads or changes a record by ID must check that the current user is allowed to access that specific record (scope the query by owner/tenant); being authenticated is not enough.

verify.description: User A requesting user B's resource by ID gets 403/404.

controls.title: Deny-by-default function-level authorization
controls.ai_rule: Apply authorization middleware to all routes by default and explicitly mark public ones; check roles/permissions on the server for every privileged action, never only in the UI.

verify.description: A regular user calling an admin endpoint gets 403.

controls.title: Validate requests against a schema and return explicit response shapes
controls.ai_rule: Validate every request with a schema that rejects unknown fields; never pass req.body directly to an ORM create/update; return explicit response objects, never whole database models.

verify.description: No ORM create/update called with the raw request body.
Sending role=admin in a profile update has no effect.

controls.title: Rate limits, pagination caps, payload limits and timeouts
controls.ai_rule: List endpoints must enforce a maximum page size; apply rate limits, request body size limits and timeouts to all API routes.

verify.description: limit=100000 is clamped; exceeding the rate limit returns 429.

controls.title: Strict CORS allow-list
controls.ai_rule: Configure CORS with an explicit list of allowed origins; never reflect the request Origin, never allow "null", and never use "*" with credentials.

verify.description: A request from https://evil.example gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

controls.title: Generic errors, no debug mode or version headers in production
controls.ai_rule: API error responses must not include stack traces, SQL errors or internal paths; return a generic message with a request ID and log details server-side; disable X-Powered-By and debug modes.

verify.description: A forced 500 error returns no stack trace.

controls.title: Keep an API inventory and retire old versions
controls.ai_rule: Document new endpoints in the API spec; do not add debug, test or temporary endpoints without removing them before merge.

verify.description: Routes in production match the documented API inventory.

controls.title: Send credentials in headers, never in URLs
controls.ai_rule: Accept API keys and tokens only from headers or cookies, never from query string parameters.

verify.description: No req.query.token / api_key / access_token reads.

threats.title: SQL injection
Excessive damage from a compromised application account
Credentials leaked from source code or images
Interception of database traffic
Exposure of sensitive data from stolen disks, snapshots or backups

controls.title: Use parameterized queries or a safe query builder / ORM
controls.ai_rule: Never build SQL with string concatenation or template literals; always use bound parameters, and pick dynamic identifiers (columns, sort order) from an allow-list.

verify.description: No query()/execute()/raw() call receives a concatenated or interpolated string.

controls.title: Load database credentials from a secret store, never from source
controls.ai_rule: Never hardcode database credentials or connection strings; read them from environment variables or a secrets manager.

verify.description: No connection string with an inline password in source files.

controls.title: Least-privilege database accounts
controls.ai_rule: The application connects with a least-privilege database user; migrations use a separate account; never connect as root/superuser/admin.

verify.description: Application DB role has no DDL/superuser rights.

controls.title: Encrypt database connections with verified TLS
controls.ai_rule: Database connections must use TLS with certificate verification; never disable certificate checks (e.g. rejectUnauthorized: false, sslmode=require without verify).

verify.description: No rejectUnauthorized false in DB client config.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in backups
controls.ai_rule: Sensitive fields (IDs, health, financial data) are encrypted at rest; keys come from a KMS, never from source code.

verify.description: Storage encryption is enabled on the DB instance and its backups.

threats.title: Upload of executable or malicious content
Path traversal through the file name
Resource exhaustion through huge files or decompression bombs
Stored XSS by serving uploads as HTML/SVG from the app origin
Malware distribution to other users

controls.title: Validate type by file content against an allow-list
controls.ai_rule: Validate uploads by file content (magic bytes) against an allow-list of types; never trust the extension or client Content-Type; re-encode images server-side.

verify.description: A PHP/HTML file renamed to .jpg is rejected.

controls.title: Generate server-side file names; never use the client file name in paths
controls.ai_rule: Store uploads under a server-generated random name; never build a filesystem path or object key from the user-supplied file name.

verify.description: No path.join / open() using the uploaded file's original name.

controls.title: Store uploads outside the web root with no execute permission
controls.ai_rule: Store uploads in private object storage or a non-executable directory outside the web root; serve them via short-lived signed URLs or a controlled download handler.

verify.description: Upload location is not reachable as a static path and buckets are private.

controls.title: Serve user files safely (separate origin, attachment, nosniff)
controls.ai_rule: Serve user uploads from a separate domain with Content-Disposition: attachment (except safe images), explicit Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; never inline user SVG/HTML on the app origin.

verify.description: Download responses include nosniff and attachment headers.

controls.title: Enforce size limits and guard against decompression bombs
controls.ai_rule: Enforce a maximum upload size at the server, and cap decompressed size, entry count and image dimensions before processing any archive or image.

verify.description: Body-size limit is configured on the upload route.
An upload above the limit returns 413.

controls.title: Scan uploaded files for malware
controls.ai_rule: Quarantine uploads and make them available to other users only after a malware scan passes.

verify.description: The upload pipeline has a scan step before files are published.

threats.title: Forged payment webhooks mark unpaid orders as paid
Price or amount tampering by the client
Double fulfilment from retries, replays or race conditions
Payment-page script tampering (Magecart-style skimming)
Card testing (carding) through the checkout
Card data leaked through logs, analytics or databases

controls.title: Verify webhook signatures and process each event once
controls.ai_rule: Payment webhooks must verify the provider signature on the raw request body with the webhook secret, reject stale timestamps, and ignore event IDs that were already processed.

verify.description: A webhook with an invalid signature returns 400 and changes nothing.

controls.title: Compute amounts on the server and verify them before fulfilment
controls.ai_rule: Never accept prices, totals or currency from the client; compute amounts on the server from the catalog and verify the paid amount and currency before fulfilling an order.

verify.description: Changing the price in the checkout request does not change the charged amount.

controls.title: Never log or store card data; keep only provider tokens and the last 4 digits
controls.ai_rule: Never log, persist or send to analytics any card number, CVV or full payment payload; store only provider IDs plus brand and last 4 digits.

verify.description: Logs and analytics events from a test checkout contain no card data.

controls.title: Idempotent payment and fulfilment operations
controls.ai_rule: Create charges with idempotency keys and make order fulfilment idempotent (unique constraint or transaction on the payment ID) so it can never run twice.

verify.description: Delivering the same payment-succeeded event twice concurrently fulfils once.

controls.title: Control and monitor scripts on payment pages
controls.ai_rule: Do not add third-party scripts to checkout pages; payment pages use a strict CSP and Subresource Integrity for every external script.

verify.description: Checkout responses carry a CSP without unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval for scripts.

controls.title: Throttle and screen payment attempts against card testing
controls.ai_rule: Rate-limit payment and card-setup attempts per user, IP and card fingerprint, and keep the provider's fraud screening enabled.

verify.description: Repeated declined attempts trigger throttling.

threats.title: Secrets committed to source control
Secrets shipped inside web bundles or mobile apps
Long-lived secrets that are never rotated
Secrets leaked through logs, error reports or CI output
Over-privileged credentials magnify any leak
CI/CD compromise exposes deployment credentials

controls.title: Never commit secrets; scan for them before every commit and in CI
controls.ai_rule: Never write real secrets, API keys or passwords into code, config or example files; read them from environment variables or a secret store and use placeholders in .env.example.

verify.description: A secret scanner runs in pre-commit and CI; .env is gitignored.

controls.title: No private secrets in client code
controls.ai_rule: Never put secret keys in frontend or mobile code, including NEXT_PUBLIC_, VITE_, EXPO_PUBLIC_ or REACT_APP_ variables; calls that need a secret must go through the backend.

verify.description: No secret-looking literals or secret env vars referenced in client code.

controls.title: Use a secrets manager in production
controls.ai_rule: Load production secrets from the configured secrets manager or environment at runtime; never read them from files committed with the code.

verify.description: Production secrets live in a managed store with access logging.

controls.title: Least-privilege credentials, separate per environment
controls.ai_rule: Use separate, minimally scoped credentials per service and per environment; never reuse production credentials in development or tests.

verify.description: Production keys have restricted scopes and are not present in dev configs.

controls.title: Redact secrets from logs, errors and CI output
controls.ai_rule: Never log or print environment variables, config objects, headers like Authorization, or any secret value; redact them in logs and error reports.

verify.description: No logging of process.env, config objects or Authorization headers.

controls.title: Rotate secrets and prefer short-lived credentials
controls.ai_rule: Design code so every secret can be rotated without a code change (read at startup or per use); prefer short-lived credentials or workload identity over static keys.

verify.description: There is a documented rotation procedure and it has been exercised.

controls.title: Harden the CI/CD pipeline
controls.ai_rule: In CI workflows: pin third-party actions to a full commit SHA, use OIDC instead of stored cloud keys, and never expose secrets to fork pull requests.

verify.description: CI workflow actions are pinned by SHA.

threats.title: Attacks go undetected because security events are not logged
Passwords, tokens or personal data written to logs
Log injection and forged log entries
Logs tampered with, deleted, or readable by too many people
Incidents discovered too late because nobody is alerted
Detailed error messages shown to users

controls.title: Log security-relevant events with enough context
controls.ai_rule: Log authentication events, authorization failures, validation failures and admin actions as structured events with timestamp, user ID, IP, request ID, action and outcome.

verify.description: A failed login and a 403 each produce a structured security log entry.

controls.title: Never log secrets or sensitive personal data
controls.ai_rule: Never log passwords, tokens, cookies, Authorization headers, card data or full request bodies; configure logger redaction for these fields.

verify.description: No logging of req.body, req.headers or password/token variables.

controls.title: Structured logging that neutralizes user input
controls.ai_rule: Use the structured logger and pass user-controlled values as separate fields, never concatenated into the log message string.

verify.description: No string concatenation of request data into log messages.

controls.title: Centralized, access-controlled, tamper-resistant log storage
controls.ai_rule: Send logs to the central log pipeline (stdout or the configured transport); do not write security logs to local files only.

verify.description: Application servers cannot delete or modify shipped logs.

controls.title: Alert on suspicious activity
controls.ai_rule: When adding security-relevant features, emit events that monitoring can alert on (auth failures, permission changes, admin actions).

verify.description: A simulated brute-force attack triggers an alert.

controls.title: Generic errors for users, details only in server logs
controls.ai_rule: Route errors through a global handler that returns a generic message with a request ID to the client and logs details server-side.

verify.description: An unhandled exception returns a generic body with a request ID.

controls.title: Retention limits and access auditing for regulated data in logs
controls.ai_rule: Log pseudonymous user IDs instead of names, emails or other personal data.

verify.description: Log retention and access policies match the applicable regulation.

threats.title: Sensitive data readable from insecure local storage
Sensitive data leaked through device logs
Sensitive data leaked through device or cloud backups
Leakage through app-switcher screenshots, clipboard or keyboard cache
Extractable encryption keys (hardcoded or stored in software)
Data left on the device after logout or account deletion

controls.title: Keep tokens and secrets in the Keychain / Android Keystore
controls.ai_rule: Store tokens and secrets only in the iOS Keychain (ThisDeviceOnly) or encrypted with an Android Keystore key; never in SharedPreferences, UserDefaults, AsyncStorage or plain files.

verify.description: No token-like keys written to SharedPreferences, UserDefaults or AsyncStorage.

controls.title: Hardware-backed, non-exportable keys; no hardcoded keys
controls.ai_rule: Generate encryption keys inside the Android Keystore or iOS Secure Enclave/Keychain; never hardcode keys or ship them in the app.

verify.description: No hardcoded key/IV byte arrays or base64 key constants.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive local databases and files
controls.ai_rule: Sensitive data stored on the device must be minimized and encrypted (SQLCipher or equivalent, iOS NSFileProtectionComplete) with keys from the Keystore/Keychain.

verify.description: Database and files pulled from a test device are not readable in plaintext.

controls.title: No sensitive data in logs; strip logging from release builds
controls.ai_rule: Never log tokens, credentials or personal data in the mobile app; wrap debug logging so it is stripped from release builds.

verify.description: No Log.d/print/console.log calls containing token, password or email variables.

controls.title: Exclude sensitive data from backups
controls.ai_rule: Exclude tokens and sensitive files from backups (Android dataExtractionRules or allowBackup=false; iOS ThisDeviceOnly Keychain items and isExcludedFromBackup).

verify.description: AndroidManifest backup settings exclude sensitive data.

controls.title: Protect sensitive screens from screenshots, clipboard and keyboard caching
controls.ai_rule: Screens showing sensitive data must hide content in the app switcher (FLAG_SECURE on Android, blur overlay on iOS); sensitive inputs disable autocorrect and suggestions.

verify.description: The app-switcher preview of sensitive screens shows no data.

controls.title: Wipe local data on logout and account deletion
controls.ai_rule: Logout must delete stored tokens, caches and the user's local files, and revoke the refresh token on the server.

verify.description: After logout, app storage contains no user data.

threats.title: Traffic read or modified because it is sent in cleartext
Man-in-the-middle because certificate validation is disabled or trusts user-installed CAs
Malicious links trigger actions or inject data into the app
Other apps abuse exported components (activities, services, receivers, providers)
Release builds that can be debugged or inspected at runtime
Known vulnerabilities in outdated platform versions
Biometric check bypassed because it only returns true/false

controls.title: Never disable certificate validation or trust user-installed CAs in release builds
controls.ai_rule: Never write trust-all TrustManagers, always-true HostnameVerifiers, disabled iOS trust evaluation, or network configs that trust user CAs outside debug-overrides — not even "temporarily".

verify.description: No trust-all TrustManager/HostnameVerifier or disabled trust evaluator.

controls.title: HTTPS only — no cleartext traffic
controls.ai_rule: Never enable cleartext HTTP in the mobile app: no usesCleartextTraffic or cleartextTrafficPermitted=true on Android, no NSAllowsArbitraryLoads or insecure ATS exceptions on iOS; use https:// URLs only.

verify.description: No cleartext permissions in AndroidManifest.xml, network security config or Info.plist.

controls.title: Treat deep links as untrusted input
controls.ai_rule: Validate every deep-link parameter; require user confirmation before acting on a link; prefer verified App Links/Universal Links over custom URL schemes for sensitive flows.

verify.description: Link handlers validate input and confirm sensitive actions.

controls.title: Export only the components that must be reachable from other apps
controls.ai_rule: New Android services, receivers and content providers use android:exported="false" unless they must be public, in which case they require a signature-level permission.

verify.description: Exported services, receivers and providers declare a permission.

controls.title: Release builds are not debuggable
controls.ai_rule: Never make release builds debuggable; guard WebView debugging and debug-only features with BuildConfig.DEBUG / #if DEBUG.

verify.description: Release build types and manifests are not debuggable.

controls.title: Bind biometric unlock to a Keystore/Keychain key
controls.ai_rule: Biometric login must unlock a cryptographic key (BiometricPrompt with a CryptoObject; a Keychain item protected by biometryCurrentSet), never just check a success callback.

verify.description: BiometricPrompt is called with a CryptoObject; no bare LAContext.evaluatePolicy for login.

controls.title: Keep platform versions current and be able to force updates
controls.ai_rule: Do not lower targetSdk or the minimum iOS version; keep build tooling and platform SDKs current.

verify.description: targetSdk is recent; a forced-update mechanism exists.

threats.title: Prompt injection (direct, or indirect through documents, emails and web pages)
Sensitive information disclosure through model output
Improper output handling (XSS, injection or code execution via model output)
System prompt leakage exposes secrets or internal logic
RAG returns documents the user may not see, or poisoned content
Unbounded consumption (denial of service and denial of wallet)
Model provider API key extracted from the client app

controls.title: Treat model input as untrusted; enforce security outside the model
controls.ai_rule: Never rely on prompt instructions for security: enforce authorization and business rules in code around the LLM call, and pass user/retrieved content as clearly delimited data.

verify.description: An "ignore previous instructions" payload cannot reach data or actions the user lacks access to.

controls.title: Treat model output as untrusted input
controls.ai_rule: Treat LLM output as untrusted: sanitize before rendering (no innerHTML or raw-HTML Markdown), validate structured output with a schema, and never eval or execute it outside a sandbox.

verify.description: Model output containing is rendered inert.

controls.title: Call the model from the backend only
controls.ai_rule: Never call the LLM provider directly from frontend or mobile code with an API key; route every call through the backend.

verify.description: No LLM SDK imports or provider API keys in client code.

controls.title: Keep secrets and other users' data out of prompts
controls.ai_rule: Never put API keys, credentials, or data the current user is not authorized to see into prompts or system prompts; assume all prompt content can be extracted.

verify.description: System prompts and context builders contain no secrets or cross-user data.

controls.title: Enforce permissions at retrieval time and vet ingested sources
controls.ai_rule: RAG retrieval must filter by the current user's tenant and permissions inside the vector query, before any content reaches the model.

verify.description: A user's question cannot retrieve another tenant's documents.

controls.title: Rate limits, token limits and spending caps
controls.ai_rule: Every LLM call must have per-user rate limiting, max input/output token limits and a timeout.

verify.description: Exceeding the per-user LLM quota returns 429.

controls.title: Minimize and protect data sent to hosted model providers
controls.ai_rule: Send the minimum data needed to the model provider and redact personal data that the feature does not need.

verify.description: Provider data-retention terms are reviewed and documented.

controls.title: Log AI interactions and tool calls for audit
controls.ai_rule: Log every LLM tool call (tool name, arguments with secrets redacted, user ID, outcome).

verify.description: Tool invocations appear in the audit log.
